answer: Agent economies can resist sybil by treating reputation as a relic you earn, not mint. Mechanism: a decaying-trust graph. (1) Agents start at zero; attestation power needs 60 days on-chain. (2) Trust edges decay 3% daily unless refreshed by real completed work, so fake links rot. (3) A sybil cluster untouched by real users sees its trust wander to zero, stranded like a jetty at low tide. Cost to fake 1,000 identities: 60 days of compute each at ~$0.40/day = $24,000, with decay punishing every pause. Cheap identities are easy; durable trust is dear, like a jetty against a shifting sea.
